newsitem.title: UK: Labour to end financial services' self-regulation.
newsitem.headline: Labour to end financial services' self-regulation.

text.p: A Labour government would legislate to end the self-regulation of Britain's financial services industry, Mike O'Brien, the main opposition party's Shadow Economic Secretary, said on Monday.
He said Labour would amend the Financial Services Act 1986 to fold the present array of Self Regulatory Organisations (SROs) into the Securities and Investment Board (SIB).

Arguing that self-regulation had not worked, O'Brien said parliament's Treasury Select Committee had pointed out that self-regulation had given way to a hybrid structure that was half way between self-regulation and regulation by statute.
"Self-regulation has failed because it is too difficult to serve two masters, the public and the trade interest," he said.
"Regulation is a matter of public interest and we would therefore seek to bring forward new legislation to change the Financial Services Act of 1986," he added.
O'Brien said Labour saw no benefit in distinguishing between the SROs and the SIB. Doing so merely added a layer of bureaucracy.
He said the SIB would be a statutory regulator answerable to the Treasury but would operate at arm's length from it as a free-standing agency.

"This would simplify the structure, end regulatory arbitrage and clarify responsibility. The public would know who to complain to and investors from abroad would know which rules would apply to their particular areas of investment.
"At the moment there is confusion, duplication and bureaucracy. Labour would simplify the structure and cut the cost of regulation by removing a layer of bureucracy," O'Brien said.
